AlphaGenome Finetuning Pipeline#

CLI-based Python scripts and shell wrappers to build and run an AlphaGenome fine-tuning pipeline and evaluate the model outputs on test intervals.

This tutorial demonstrates how to fine-tune the heads of an AlphaGenome model from previously prepared BigWig files (see the Model Input Generation Pipeline guide). Heads must be fine-tuned following the 4-fold split defined in the original paper. This example shows how to train a single fold. For accurate predictions, models should be trained on all four folds and their predictions averaged.

Non-zero Mean Computation#

Assuming base-resolution BigWig (.bw) files are already generated for all modalities, we first need to compute the non-zero track mean for proper input scaling. This is handled directly in bash.

Computes the mean of non-zero track values for BigWig files, specifically restricted to canonical chromosomes (chr1-22, X).

  • Input: $1 - Directory containing input .bw files

  • Output: $2 - CSV file capturing basename, non-zero mean, and full path

src/AlphaGenome_finetuning/00_compute_nonzero_means_per_bw.sh#
 1#!/bin/bash
 2# ==============================================================================
 3# Code by Jakob Then
 4# 
 5# Purpose: Computes the mean of non-zero track values for BigWig (.bw) files, 
 6#          specifically restricted to canonical chromosomes (chr1-22, X, Y). 
 7#          Designed for AlphaGenome finetuning data preparation.
 8# Input:   $1 - Directory containing input .bw files
 9# Output:  $2 - CSV file capturing basename, non-zero mean, and full path
10# ==============================================================================
11
12# SLURM Configuration
13#SBATCH --job-name=bw_mean_calc
14#SBATCH --output=logs/bw_mean_%j.log
15#SBATCH --error=logs/bw_mean_%j.err
16#SBATCH --time=04:00:00          # Adjust depending on the total number of BigWig files
17#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1        # Sequential processing per file
18#SBATCH --mem=64G                # Allocated generously to load large chromosome arrays into memory safely
19#SBATCH --partition=bigmem       # Ensure this matches your specific cluster topology
20
21# Example usage:
22# sbatch 00_compute_nonzero_means_per_bw.sh input_data/AlphaGenome_Borzoi_input input_data/metadata/bw_nonzero_means.csv
23
24source /g/easybuild/x86_64/Rocky/8/haswell/software/Miniforge3/24.1.2-0/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
25#source env/initiate_alphagenome_ft_env.sh
26source /g/steinmetz/projects/variant2function_project/env/alphagenome_ft//initiate_alphagenome_ft_env.sh
27
28# Validate CLI arguments to prevent empty variable execution errors
29if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
30    echo "Usage: sbatch $0 <input_directory> <output_file.csv>"
31    exit 1
32fi
33
34INPUT_DIR="$1"
35OUTPUT_FILE="$2"
36
37echo "Starting job on $(date)"
38echo "Input directory: $INPUT_DIR"
39echo "Output file: $OUTPUT_FILE"
40
41echo "basename,nonzero_mean_canonical,full_path" > "$OUTPUT_FILE"
42
43# Iterate through all BigWig files in the target directory
44find "$INPUT_DIR" -type f -name "*.bw" | while read -r bw_file; do
45    
46    base_name=$(basename "$bw_file")
47    
48    # Calculate non-zero means using an inline Python script. 
49    nonzero_mean=$(python3 -c '
50import sys, pyBigWig, numpy as np
51
52# Restrict analysis strictly to canonical chromosomes to prevent skewed means from alt-contigs or unplaced scaffolds
53valid_chroms = set([f"chr{i}" for i in range(1, 23)] + ["chrX", "chrY"])
54
55try:
56    bw = pyBigWig.open(sys.argv[1])
57    total_sum = 0
58    total_count = 0
59    
60    for chrom, length in bw.chroms().items():
61        if chrom not in valid_chroms:
62            continue
63            
64        # Load chromosome values into a numpy array for fast, vectorized filtering
65        vals = bw.values(chrom, 0, length, numpy=True)
66        
67        # Filter out zeroes and NaN values (unmapped regions)
68        nz = vals[(vals != 0) & (~np.isnan(vals))]
69        
70        total_sum += nz.sum()
71        total_count += len(nz)
72        
73    mean_val = total_sum / total_count if total_count > 0 else "NaN"
74    print(mean_val)
75    bw.close()
76except Exception as e:
77    print("Error_Reading_File")
78' "$bw_file")
79
80    # Append results incrementally to prevent data loss if the SLURM job times out unexpectedly
81    echo "$base_name,$nonzero_mean,$bw_file" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
82    echo "Processed: $base_name"
83done
84
85conda deactivate
86echo "Job finished on $(date). Results saved to $OUTPUT_FILE"

1. Config File Generation#

Next, we create a .yaml configuration file specifying the tracks and heads to fine-tune.

We specify a directory and modality subfolders corresponding to the output heads. This Python script loads all .bw files in the directory as tracks for the heads and generates a configuration .yaml file. This file is used every time we initialize the model to attach the fine-tuned heads to the pre-trained trunk.

Python script:

Generate AG finetuning YAML config

usage: make_AG_input_config.py [-h] --data_dir DATA_DIR
                               [--config_prefix CONFIG_PREFIX]
                               --modality_folders MODALITY_FOLDERS [MODALITY_FOLDERS ...]
                               [--nonzero_means NONZERO_MEANS]
                               [--norm_tag NORM_TAG]

Named Arguments#

--data_dir

Base path to bigwig input data directories

--config_prefix

Path and name of the output YAML file

Default: 'config.yaml'

--modality_folders

List of subfolders in data_dir corresponding to modalities. Must contain ATAC, RNA, or CutnTag in name.

--nonzero_means

CSV file generated by 00_compute_nonzero_means_per_bw.sh

Default: 'input_data/metadata/bw_nonzero_means.csv'

--norm_tag

Tag to filter and clean normalized bigwig files (default: None)

Alternatively, we can use a bash wrapper to execute the Python config generator.

  • Input: Hardcoded variables pointing to directories and metadata

  • Output: A formatted .yaml configuration file (e.g., test_config.yaml)

src/AlphaGenome_finetuning/01_make_config_file.sh#
 1#!/bin/bash
 2# ==============================================================================
 3# Code by Jakob Then
 4# 
 5# Purpose: Wrapper script to execute the Python config generator for 
 6#          AlphaGenome finetuning. It feeds predefined paths and modality
 7#          lists into the Python parser to generate the final YAML.
 8# Input:   Hardcoded variables pointing to directories and metadata
 9# Output:  A formatted .yaml configuration file (e.g., test_config.yaml)
10# ==============================================================================
11
12# SLURM Configuration
13#SBATCH --job-name=make_config
14#SBATCH --output=logs/make_config_%j.log 
15#SBATCH --error=logs/make_config_%j.err
16#SBATCH --time=01:00:00          
17#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1        # Sequential processing per file
18#SBATCH --mem=16G                
19#SBATCH --partition=bigmem       # Ensure this matches your specific cluster topology
20
21# Setup core paths and variables
22TARGETS_CONFIG_PATH="configs/test_config.yaml"
23DATA_DIR="../../input_data/AlphaGenome_Borzoi_input"
24NONZERO_MEANS_PATH="../../input_data/bw_nonzero_means.csv"
25#folders in DATA_DIR
26MODALITIES=(
27    "multiome_RNA_3prime_bigwig_deduplicated" 
28    "multiome_ATAC_bigwig_deduplicated" 
29    "CutnTag_bigwig"
30)
31
32# Load conda environments
33source /g/easybuild/x86_64/Rocky/8/haswell/software/Miniforge3/24.1.2-0/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
34source env/initiate_alphagenome_ft_env.sh
35
36# Execute the Python config builder
37python ../utils/preprocessing/make_AG_input_config.py \
38    --data_dir "${DATA_DIR}" \
39    --config_prefix "${TARGETS_CONFIG_PATH}" \
40    --modality_folders "${MODALITIES[@]}" \
41    --norm_tag "_100M" \
42    --nonzero_means "${NONZERO_MEANS_PATH}"
43
44conda deactivate

2. Fine-tuning#

After the configuration file is generated, we can begin fine-tuning our AlphaGenome model. The fine-tuning is handled by the following script:

AlphaGenome Finetuning Script

usage: finetune_heads.py [-h] --fasta_path FASTA_PATH --config CONFIG
                         --base_dir BASE_DIR --checkpoint_dir CHECKPOINT_DIR
                         [--fold FOLD] [--window_size WINDOW_SIZE]
                         [--organism ORGANISM] [--model_version MODEL_VERSION]
                         [--batch_size BATCH_SIZE] [--epochs EPOCHS] [--lr LR]
                         [--weight_decay WEIGHT_DECAY] [--seed SEED]
                         [--patience PATIENCE] [--min_delta MIN_DELTA]

Named Arguments#

--fasta_path

Path to the genome.fa file

--config

Path to the target YAML config file

--base_dir

Base directory for resolving config paths (e.g., the local tmp dir)

--checkpoint_dir

Directory to save checkpoints

--fold

Data fold to use (0, 1, 2, 3)

Default: '1'

--window_size

Window size in bp (default: 1 Mbp)

Default: 1048576

--organism

Target organism

Default: 'HOMO_SAPIENS'

--model_version

Base model version (e.g., fold_1, all_folds)

Default: 'fold_1'

--batch_size

Global batch size (must be divisible by N_GPUs)

Default: 16

--epochs

Number of training epochs

Default: 10

--lr

Learning rate

Default: 0.0003

--weight_decay

Weight decay

Default: 0.01

--seed

Random seed

Default: 42

--patience

Early stopping patience

Default: 5

--min_delta

Early stopping min delta

Default: 0.0

To make this run quickly on any cluster, it is highly recommended to stage the BigWig data to the tmp directory of the GPU node before starting the fine-tuning.

We can do this with the following helper script, which stages the .bw files specified in the config.yaml from the input directory to a tmp directory on the node. It also generates a new config.yaml in the tmp directory with updated data paths pointing to the staged .bw files.

Stage AlphaGenome data to local tmp and update YAML config.

usage: stage_to_tmp.py [-h] --master_yaml MASTER_YAML --tmp_dir TMP_DIR
                       [--out_yaml OUT_YAML]

Named Arguments#

--master_yaml

Path to the input master YAML config

--tmp_dir

Path to the local tmp directory on the compute node

--out_yaml

Path for the output temporary YAML (defaults to <tmp_dir>/tmp_bw_config.yaml)

As an example, this bash script can be used to execute the entire data staging and fine-tuning process on a SLURM cluster:

src/AlphaGenome_finetuning/02_submit_finetune_heads.sh#
  1#!/bin/bash
  2# ==============================================================================
  3# Code by Jakob Then
  4# 
  5# Purpose: Wrapper script to finetune heads in AlphaGenome. Stages data to a temporary 
  6#          directory on the GPU node for highly accelerated data loading.
  7# Input:   Hardcoded variables pointing to bigwig directories, metadata, 
  8#          and the input config file.
  9# Output:  Checkpoints for the best and last model epoch saved to OUTPUT_DIR.
 10# ==============================================================================
 11
 12# SLURM Configuration
 13#SBATCH -J AG_finetune_heads        
 14#SBATCH -N 1                        # Single node for 8-GPU training
 15#SBATCH -p gpu-training             
 16#SBATCH --qos=high
 17#SBATCH --gpus=8                    
 18#SBATCH --cpus-per-gpu=8       
 19#SBATCH --mem-per-gpu=180G          
 20#SBATCH -C ("gpu=B200"|"gpu=H200"|"gpu=H100"|"gpu=A100")  
 21#SBATCH -t 6-00:00:00               # 6-day maximum runtime limit 
 22#SBATCH --output=logs/finetune_heads_%j.out
 23#SBATCH --error=logs/finetune_heads_%j.err
 24
 25# Setup core paths and training hyperparameters
 26DATA_DIR="../../input_data/AlphaGenome_Borzoi_input"
 27OUTPUT_DIR="../../models/AlphaGenome_ft"
 28INPUT_CONFIG_FILE="configs/simple_merged_deduplicated.yaml"
 29GENOME_FASTA="../../input_data/metadata/GRCh38_gencode_release29_genome_fasta/genome.fa"
 30
 31# Dynamically assign a node-local temp directory based on the unique Slurm job ID
 32LOCAL_TMP_DIR="/tmp/alphagenome_bws_${SLURM_JOB_ID}" #adjust to node tmp dir if needed
 33
 34BATCH_SIZE=16  # Represents 2 intervals per GPU. Adjust if out-of-memory errors occur, but fine for H100s. Must be a multiple of n_GPUS
 35MAX_EPOCHS=10 
 36
 37echo "======================================================"
 38echo "Starting AlphaGenome Finetuning Job"
 39echo "======================================================"
 40echo "Date:           $(date)"
 41echo "User:           $(whoami)"
 42echo "Job ID:         ${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
 43echo "Execution Node: ${SLURMD_NODENAME}"
 44echo "======================================================"
 45echo ""
 46
 47# Load Conda environment
 48source /g/easybuild/x86_64/Rocky/8/haswell/software/Miniforge3/24.1.2-0/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
 49source /g/steinmetz/projects/variant2function_project/env/alphagenome_ft/initiate_alphagenome_ft_env.sh
 50#source ../../env/initiate_alphagenome_ft_env.sh
 51
 52# Confirm correct JAX and CUDA setup before we start copying massive files
 53bash ../../env/test_alphagenome_ft_env_config.sh
 54
 55# Enable XLA autotune caching. This benchmarks operations on the specific GPU 
 56# architecture to find the fastest execution paths, saving time on restarts.
 57export XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_per_fusion_autotune_cache_dir=xla_cache"
 58
 59# ==============================================================================
 60# I/O OPTIMIZATION: Node-local Data Staging
 61# ==============================================================================
 62
 63# ALWAYS clean up the local /tmp directory when the script exits
 64trap 'echo "Cleaning up node-local tmp directory..."; rm -rf "${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}"; echo "Cleanup complete."' EXIT
 65
 66mkdir -p "${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}"
 67
 68# Stage genome .fa and its .fai index.
 69echo "Staging Genome files to ${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}..."
 70rsync -a "${GENOME_FASTA}"* "${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}"/
 71
 72# Stage BigWig files and generate a new temporary YAML config that points
 73# the model to the local /tmp/ paths instead of the slow network drive.
 74echo "Staging BigWig files and generating temp YAML..."
 75LOCAL_YAML="${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}/running_config.yaml"
 76python ../utils/finetuning/AlphaGenome/stage_to_tmp.py \
 77    --master_yaml "${INPUT_CONFIG_FILE}" \
 78    --tmp_dir "${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}" \
 79    --out_yaml "${LOCAL_YAML}"
 80
 81# ==============================================================================
 82# MODEL TRAINING
 83# ==============================================================================
 84
 85echo "Starting model finetuning..."
 86# Using srun here ensures proper CPU/GPU binding and resource distribution within the allocated SLURM step.
 87srun python ../utils/finetuning/AlphaGenome/finetune_heads.py \
 88    --fasta_path "${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}/genome.fa" \
 89    --config "${LOCAL_YAML}" \
 90    --base_dir "${LOCAL_TMP_DIR}" \
 91    --checkpoint_dir "${OUTPUT_DIR}" \
 92    --batch_size $BATCH_SIZE \
 93    --epochs $MAX_EPOCHS \
 94    --lr 3e-4
 95
 96# Cleanup
 97conda deactivate
 98
 99echo ""
100echo "======================================================"
101echo "Training done! Ending job on: $(date)"
102echo "======================================================"

In cases where fine-tuning fails or is aborted (due to a low max epoch count, timeout errors, etc.), or if the user desires iterative fine-tuning with altered learning rates, loss weights, or additional unfrozen layers, we created a resume fine-tuning script. This allows you to restart the fine-tuning from an existing model checkpoint.

Caution: This script currently resets optimizer states (parameters optimized during validation steps) and only loads weights and biases. Expect small spikes in loss during the first few epochs.

AlphaGenome Resume Finetuning Script

usage: resume_finetune_heads.py [-h] --fasta_path FASTA_PATH --config CONFIG
                                --base_dir BASE_DIR
                                --in_checkpoint_dir IN_CHECKPOINT_DIR
                                --out_checkpoint_dir OUT_CHECKPOINT_DIR
                                [--fold FOLD] [--window_size WINDOW_SIZE]
                                [--organism ORGANISM]
                                [--model_version MODEL_VERSION]
                                [--batch_size BATCH_SIZE] [--epochs EPOCHS]
                                [--lr LR] [--weight_decay WEIGHT_DECAY]
                                [--seed SEED] [--patience PATIENCE]
                                [--min_delta MIN_DELTA]

Named Arguments#

--fasta_path

Path to the genome.fa file

--config

Path to the target YAML config file

--base_dir

Base directory for resolving config paths (e.g., the local tmp dir)

--in_checkpoint_dir

Directory containing the checkpoint to resume from

--out_checkpoint_dir

Directory to save new checkpoints

--fold

Data fold to use (0, 1, 2, 3)

Default: '1'

--window_size

Window size in bp (default: 1 Mbp)

Default: 1048576

--organism

Target organism

Default: 'HOMO_SAPIENS'

--model_version

Base model version (e.g., fold_1, all_folds)

Default: 'fold_1'

--batch_size

Global batch size (must be divisible by N_GPUs)

Default: 16

--epochs

Number of training epochs

Default: 10

--lr

Learning rate

Default: 0.0003

--weight_decay

Weight decay

Default: 0.01

--seed

Random seed

Default: 42

--patience

Early stopping patience

Default: 5

--min_delta

Early stopping min delta

Default: 0.0

An example of a full bash wrapper for resuming a job can be found at: ../../src/AlphaGenome_finetuning/02b_resume_submit_finetune_heads.sh

3. Fine-tuning Evaluation#

After fine-tuning is complete, we need to ensure its success by assessing the model’s predictions on its test intervals. To avoid having to store all output predictions (which can exceed 1TB at 1bp resolution as compressed .h5 files), the correlation is computed in a streamed manner while making forward passes, keeping a running sum for every batch of outputs.

This script integrates the evaluation pipeline (shared across models, found at ../../src/utils/eval) with AlphaGenome forward passes.

AlphaGenome Finetuned Streaming Evaluation Script

usage: evaluate_AG_on_test_streamed.py [-h] --fasta_path FASTA_PATH
                                       --config CONFIG --input_dir INPUT_DIR
                                       --out_dir OUT_DIR
                                       --checkpoint_dir CHECKPOINT_DIR
                                       [--gtf_file GTF_FILE] [--fold FOLD]
                                       [--window_size WINDOW_SIZE]
                                       [--organism ORGANISM]
                                       [--model_version MODEL_VERSION]
                                       [--batch_size BATCH_SIZE]
                                       [--resolution RESOLUTION]
                                       [--save_predictions SAVE_PREDICTIONS]
                                       [--minimal_test MINIMAL_TEST]

Named Arguments#

--fasta_path

Path to the genome.fa file

--config

Path to the target YAML config file

--input_dir

Directory containing input BigWig files

--out_dir

Output directory for figures and results

--checkpoint_dir

Directory containing the best model checkpoint

--gtf_file

Optional GTF file for Gene-based correlation mapping

--fold

Data fold to use (0, 1, 2, 3)

Default: '1'

--window_size

Window size in bp (must map to an AlphaGenome config)

Default: 1048576

--organism

Target organism

Default: 'HOMO_SAPIENS'

--model_version

Base model version (e.g., fold_1, all_folds)

Default: 'fold_1'

--batch_size

Global batch size (must be divisible by N_GPUs)

Default: 16

--resolution

Embedding resolution to evaluate (1, 128)

Default: '1'

--save_predictions

Whether to save test interval predictions to HDF5.

Default: False

--minimal_test

Truncate run to the first 8 intervals for quick debugging.

Default: False

To speed up computation, this can be integrated with data staging (just like the fine-tuning step) using a bash script like this:

src/AlphaGenome_finetuning/03_submit_test_eval.sh#

  2# ==============================================================================

  6#          heads in AlphaGenome on test intervals. Stages data to a temporary
  7#          directory on the GPU node for highly accelerated data loading. Make
  8#          forward passes on batches of test intervals and simulatanouesly computes
  9#          correaltion and other evaluation metrics using streaming accumulators to
 10#          avoid out-of-mem issues and saving 1TB of tmp data.
 11# Input:   Hardcoded variables pointing to bigwig directories, metadata, 
 12#          and the input config file plus best finetuning chepoint.

100    --minimal_test False
